title: Raindrops Are Not Teardrops
hook: Raindrops are not shaped like teardrops, even though everyone draws them that way.
script: Raindrops are not shaped like teardrops, even though everyone draws them that way. Small drops are very nearly a perfect sphere, but bigger ones get flattened like a hamburger bun. The biggest drops fall at about twenty miles an hour. So what is squashing them on the way down? Air resistance pushes up on the bottom of the falling drop. If a drop grows too large, it tears itself apart into smaller drops. So why does everyone draw a teardrop? Because a drop hanging from a tap really does look that way, just before it falls.
